meta.source: FDOT District 7, Traffic Signals Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) Reference Guide, v1.5, June 2025. PDF pages 5-11, text by pdfplumber.
meta.not_in_this_file: Damage assessment pages and Appendix A (Field Checklist) are not included. Appendix B (Hurricane Response Zone Maps, PDF p. 24) and Appendix C (Responsibility Matrix, PDF p. 25) are blank in v1.5.

weights.must: shall / must / ensure / do not / a hard deadline (within N hours)
weights.consider: consider / may / as needed / if necessary

clauses.text: Ensure eSTORM is fully updated.
Test the application to confirm all new signals are added.
Include speed feedback signs and flashers in addition to signals to aid in the Situational Awareness Team (SAT) and Damage Assessment Team (DAT) response.
Conduct eSTORM and eSTORM Lite training sessions and verify user access for all necessary staff.
Provide training for both SAT and DAT personnel, along with FDOT and consultant staffing
Print out a list of current traffic signals in eSTORM, eSTORM checklist, and eSTORM user guide.
Provide eSTORM (Lite) access to local agencies and eSTORM (regular) access to CEI staff and inspectors.
Pre-Event Contract Meeting
Review the contracting mechanism and confirm appropriate pay items. These are typically Z-Contracts or Permanent Signal Repair or Generator Deployments.
Supplement or create additional H Contracts with Temporary and Permanent Repair Pay Items under Construction to assist with volume of work and resources.
Meet with both CEI Leadership and Key Staff and provide sample Daily Work Orders and invoice deliverables with set expectations by Contract Managers.
Meet with Z-Contractors and H-Contractors and provide Invoice Samples for expeditious approvals. Use examples of past contracts.
Prepare/confirm list of SAT and DAT personnel. Compile phone numbers and email addresses.
Pre-determine deployment corridors for the following signal assessment and generator deployment teams. Coordinate with FDOT and maintaining agencies.
Print out route maps, list of contacts, and SLD, if necessary.
Identify signals located within construction projects.
Ensure signal inventory list is up to date.
Obtain cyber keys, or special keys if No. 2 keys are not utilized, from each agency.
Test all generators to confirm they are operational.
Ensure generators have proper cables.
Use combination locks on generators for secure deployments.
Consider adding geotags to generators to track location in real time. Or, consider QA Code designations for each generator to be updated for location and refueling.
Determine method for capturing and storing GPS coordinates.
Consider use of mobile apps or devices with embedded geotagging (e.g., Solocator) capabilities
Ensure all personnel are trained in the chosen method.
Utilize a streamlined group messaging option, such as WhatsApp or GroupMe, to create a text group for all key personnel to enable real-time communication before, during, and after the storm
Ensure employee access to ERS, InService, and eSTORM mailbox
Check food storage
Purchase water and non-perishable foods as needed
Conduct kickoff meetings for applicable personnel and agencies.
Conduct training trainings for contractors on generator connection procedures with difference across local agencies. Remind Contractors/CEI to take photos of the damage and repairs with context.
Contractor and Agency Coordination
Contact all contractors to confirm emergency contact details.
Conduct outreach to all maintaining agencies and coordinate post event response plans and preferences.
Verify that all appropriate parties have access to eSTORM and other agencies applications.
Provide power company and utilities contact information.
Tracking and Documentation
Distribute signal and damage tracking spreadsheet via shared link. Provide read-only access to the tracking spreadsheet for SAT assignments, generator deployments, and construction activities.
Consider housing a contractor representative in the EOC or Tampa Operations.
Obtain contractor pay item list.

Initiate and ramp up the deployment plan in coordination with field teams as storm track becomes clearer. Send notification emails to personnel outlining expected roles, reporting times, and deployment locations.
Review which agencies have generators plugs and provide ‘How-To’ guidance for their use.
Consider pre-positioning 5-8 generators in Pinellas County, Hillsborough County, and the City of Tamp for their immediate deployment at key, priority intersections.
Reserve hotels for personnel as needed.
At the RTMC, check the building for leaks. Ensure generators are operational.
Discuss tolling suspension plans in case of emergency evacuations.
Preapprove website update for toll suspension/Governor Order
Test CCTV camera feeds and user log ins at the EOC level.
Monitor arterial network and implement evacuation/revised timings at congested locations.
FDOT to assign inspectors to each generator group and/or corridor.
Tentatively assign Situational Awareness Teams (SAT) to designated corridors
Identify backup personnel in case team members are unable to deploy due to storm.
Reallocate generators from Tampa Yard to Pinellas Yard as appropriate.
Prioritize generators to Pinellas County and other agencies, as necessary.
Determine prepositioning of crews
Request Funding: Seek pre-event funding approval from the D7 District Maintenance Engineer
Fuel and load generator onto trailers. Inspectors and FDOT to track NH #’s. Key or combinations to be provided by FDOT/CEI.
Provide traffic operations personnel at Pinellas County TMC and other agencies, as necessary.
Determine number of crews and when to deploy to field (to be determined by operations centers). Provide at least 6-hour notice for all crews.
Confirm routes, ensure generators are fueled, and verify all teams are prepared.
Recheck the 48-hour item decisions.
FDOT to provide finalized deployment routes to all generator teams and SAT based on where the storm hits.
Contact maintaining agencies to verify system status via ATMS signal system. Update eSTORM accordingly based on system checks.

Once systems checks are completed and eSTORM is updated, arterial RTMC personnel to reorder, prioritize, and distribute all hurricane response zone maps, including identifying priority routes, corridors, and zones for response efforts.

TMC personnel to determine generator deployment priorities, including whether generator teams are to deploy only at Priority #1 intersections or to all non-operational signals within their assigned zones.
Generator teams and SAT on standby for immediate deployment.
Use ATMS signal system to determine what corridors are functional, meaning the signal is actively communicating with the ATMS signal system.
If a signal is functioning within the ATMS signal system, the signal symbol will appear green.
This indicates the signal is actively communicating and operational.
All operational (green) signals in the ATMS signal system should be fully reflected in eSTORM.
Signals shown as yellow or red, meaning a signal is in flash or non-operational, respectively, and should be evaluated for further action.
A yellow or red status in the ATMS signal system should be used to help prioritize SAT and generator deployment teams.
Conduct an initial windshield survey of corridors. Utilize SATs and Local Agency input.
SAT deployment teams to conduct the initial pass of all roadways immediately post storm, utilizing eSTORM Lite to document and report all findings.
Generator Deployment and Management
Assign generators to teams and document: team name, generator NH #, and time/date deployed.
Develop an ongoing refueling schedule based on fueling needs.
First refueling to occur six (6) hours after initial deployment
Status Updates and Coordination
Monitor intersections transitioning from generator power to commercial power. Use outage maps provided by power companies.
Coordinate with agencies for local generator deployment and FDOT generator replacement.
Track generator pickups and redeployments. Ensure proper check-in of generators returning to the yard.
Operational Checks utilizing ATMS signal system. Confirm signals are operating correctly upon power restoration. Report any signals in flash or not functioning properly.
Situational Awareness Team (SAT)
Deploy SAT to intersections and follow assigned corridors. SAT assessments will continue twice daily at 9:00 AM and 2:00 PM, as intermittent commercial power restoration is ongoing.
Maintain share repair/tracking spreadsheet for ongoing coordination.
Provide continuous updates on repair progress and issues encountered. eSTORM updates shall be made as soon as possible.
Detailed assessments, including pictures of damage with GPS locations.
Deploy DAT personnel. Consider requesting them to report signals, speed feedback signs, and beacons that are not found in eSTORM.
Coordinate with the local agencies on repairs and equipment needs.
Additional Notes
Ensure all teams have access to necessary templates and tracking sheets.
Maintain clear and consistent communication across all response teams utilizing a streamlined group messaging option, such as WhatsApp or GroupMe
Adjust deployment and repair strategies based on real-time field conditions.
Consider using runners to investigate field requests.
eSTORM to be constantly updated through the entire process to ensure Central Office is seeing the most up-to-date information.
Download eSTORM data each hour to keep historical track of changes.
Provide continuous updates on repair progress and issues encountered.
Track generator pickups and redeployments. Reconcile between CEI check-in and FDOT NH #’s.
Ensure proper check-in of generators returning to the yard.
Daily status update conferences
Monitor intersections transitioning from generator power to commercial power.
Refueling generators
SAT assessments shall continue daily at 9:00 AM and 2:00 PM to verify status of commercial power restoration.
As corridors are restored to commercial power, SATs can be modified to adjust resource needs.
Reduce the number of refueling teams as signals transition back to commercial power.
Conduct districtwide damage assessments using ArcGIS Field Maps/eSTORM and/or Survey123.
Load all damage, including sign-related damage, into the Damage Assessment Collector App
Upload and organize all damage pictures (Major Street @ Minor Street)
Additional Funding Request
Filter and sort the new Damage Report to determine rough estimates for repairs.
Identify repair types and costs based on the following: emergency or permanent repairs, < $5,000 or => $5,000 making sure to sum all repairs and totals
If additional funds are needed for repairs,
Request pre-event funding approvals from D7 District Maintenance Engineer DDIR Requests and Central Office as indicated in the “48 Hours Prior to Storm Event” Pre-Storm Section.
Email D7 with previous request/approval email chain.
Load request into Central Office SharePoint site as a “NEW” request. Do not edit existing requests.
Check the green arrow after the request is loaded.
TWOs to be issued once a State of Emergency is ordered for the area and funding has been programmed or appropriated. Obtain a copy of the official TWO and any extensions.
Confirm FPIDs are issued and programmed.
This will typically happen either concurrently with or immediately after the issuance of the emergency TWO depending on the urgency and type of work involved.
Issue all Emergency (both Temporary and Permanent) Work Orders.
Understand when emergency permanent repairs can be issued.
Coordinate with DDIR team to determine what grouping is required.
Email list of emergency DDIR requests to DDIR team after issuance of emergency TWOs.
Confirm FPIDs are issued and programmed.
Once funding request is approved by D7 and CO, begin to issue emergency TWOs.
After TWOs are issued and when available, enter DDIR and FPID numbers into TWOs.
Encumber funds in CFM against applicable FPIDs within 24 hours.
Track, inspect, and close.
Pay invoice and email final bill to DDIR team.
Do not issue emergency TWO after expiration of governor’s executive order.
Identify all emergency and permanent repairs (per Object ID or grouped within ¼ mile) with a repair cost of $5000 or greater.
Email a DDIR request to DDIR team for both emergency and permanent repairs.

Emergency and permanent repairs within the same Object ID or grouped with ¼ mile may be included in the same DDIR if the total cost exceeds $5,000. The DDIR must distinguish between emergency work and permanent repairs.
Once DDIRs are approved, take list to Work Program for team to issue FPIDs for emergency and/or permanent repairs.
After DDIR-related FPIDs are issued, wait for approval of DDIR by FHWA. Log the DDIR and FPIDs with each TWO in the tracking spreadsheet.
Draft the permanent TWOs and determine total repair costs for each FPID.
Program (Work Program) and encumber funds (CFM) against applicable FPIDs.
Issue permanent TWOs and copy in DDIR team.
Track, inspect, and close Permanent TWOs.
Pay invoice and email final bill to DDIR team.
Email all TWOs and include DDIR team so they are aware of pending costs and can track repairs.
Give final contract repair costs to DDIR team upon final acceptance of both emergency and permanent TWOs.
After funding request is approved by D7 and CO, begin to gather DDIR and FPIDs for permanent TWOs.
Draft the permanent TWOs and determine total repair costs for each FPID.
Encumber funds against applicable FPIDs.
Issue permanent TWOs and cc DDIR team.
Track, inspect, close.
Pay invoice and email final bill to DDIR team.
Do not issue emergency TWO after expiration of governor’s executive order.
